one_line: Sponsored walkthrough of Apify's $1M actor-building challenge (Nov 2025 to Jan 31 2026), showing how Claude Code plus Apify's agent prompt and CLI can produce a publishable actor quickly.
summary: This is a sponsored video from the AI LABS channel promoting Apify's actor-building challenge, which runs from November 3, 2025 to January 31, 2026. Participants can publish up to five "actors" (Apify's hosted, containerized automations with a typed input and structured output) and are paid by monthly active users plus a top-three judged prize. The host says Apify ships a ready-made AI-coding prompt and an MCP-server template, which lets an agent drive the Apify CLI to write, test and upload an actor. He demonstrates this with Claude Code building a Google Maps lead-generation scraper that needs a Google API key, and returned 17 results for a test query. He then lists what an actor needs before it can be published (a deployed build, README, input schema, categories, SEO, a working demo) and what the publisher needs (profile and billing details). The video is mostly prize and sign-up pitch, and the technical content stays at the level of "the agent did it" with no code, commands or failure cases shown.

key_ideas.idea: The video is sponsored by Apify, and the core message is a time-limited prize challenge rather than a technical lesson.
key_ideas.detail: The challenge started November 3 (2025) and ends January 31, 2026. The host says a partnership exists and points viewers to a sign-up link and a Discord channel with Apify staff and a Q&A session.

key_ideas.idea: Prize money is tied to real usage of published actors, not only to the judged top prizes.
key_ideas.detail: The top three are judged, with $30,000 for first place. Other money is paid at $2 per monthly active user of each actor, so 1,000 users gives a maximum of $2,000 per actor. Up to five actors count, and there is also a $2,000 weekly prize.

key_ideas.idea: An Apify actor is a Docker container that holds your code, which Apify hosts. It takes a defined input and returns structured output.
key_ideas.detail: The host describes actors as the unit of an automation. Some crawl websites and others launch a separate browser. Apify provides code templates for both developers and AI-assisted builders.

key_ideas.idea: Apify has written its docs as an AI-coding instruction set, so the user does not need to hand-build a context file.
key_ideas.detail: The host contrasts this with the usual workflow of reading the docs and writing a CLAUDE.md-style context file. The provided prompt references the Apify CLI, which gives the agent control over local writing, testing and uploading.

key_ideas.idea: A plain-language request to Claude Code is enough to generate a working actor.
key_ideas.detail: The host pastes Apify's prompt into Claude Code, asks for a Google Maps scraper, and the agent produces the full actor. The CLI pushes the project and returns a link to the actor in the Apify console.

key_ideas.idea: Publishing needs both actor-side and account-side requirements to be met.
key_ideas.detail: Actor side: deployed, a comprehensive README, a configured input schema, assigned categories, SEO, and a working demo. Account side: basic details, a public profile, and billing information so revenue can be paid out.

key_ideas.idea: Apify publishes a list of wanted actors with target audiences, which the host uses as an idea source.
key_ideas.detail: The host built a Gemini MCP actor from one of those ideas. He says anyone can adapt the listed ideas, and the templates are another starting point.

techniques.name: Template to agent prompt to CLI deploy
techniques.how: Open the Apify actor template and go to its 'use locally' section to find the command that creates an actor. Copy Apify's AI-coding prompt into Claude Code. Describe the desired actor in plain language, such as 'a Google Maps scraper that generates leads'. The agent writes the actor, tests it locally with the Apify CLI, and pushes it to Apify. The CLI returns a console link. The transcript does not show the exact create command or CLI flags.
techniques.when: Building a small scraper or automation actor quickly, without hand-writing the Apify project scaffold or context file.

techniques.name: Actor publish checklist
techniques.how: Before publishing, check the actor: deployed build, a README, a configured input schema, categories assigned, SEO fields filled in, and a working demo run. On the account side, complete the profile and billing details. Only then publish the actor to the store.
techniques.when: Preparing an Apify actor for public listing, or any agent-built tool whose users will need documentation and a working example.

techniques.name: Idea sourcing from published wish lists
techniques.how: Use Apify's public idea page, which lists actors that should exist along with their target audience. Adapt one of them, or start from a template and extend it.
techniques.when: Choosing what to build when you need a demand signal for a new actor or tool.

tools: Apify (actor platform, Apify Store, Apify console)
Google Maps (scraper input requires a Google API key)
Gemini MCP (actor built by the host)

numbers.claim: Challenge prize pool is $1 million, with $30,000 for first place and a $2,000 weekly prize.
Payout is $2 per monthly active user per actor. At 1,000 users, that is a maximum of $2,000 per actor, with up to five actors per participant.
The example Google Maps scraper actor has about 11,000 monthly active users and about 200,000 total users (host's figures, not verified in the video).
The test run of the Google Maps scraper returned 17 results for the chosen area.
Challenge window: started November 3 (2025), ends January 31, 2026.

hot_takes: Sponsored promotion. The content is mainly a prize pitch, and the host is an Apify partner. Quality is capped at 2 under the sponsored-segment rule.
The 'AI built it for you' demo shows only a happy path: one prompt, one 17-result scrape, no failures or debugging. Reliability and maintenance are not discussed.
Revenue claims ($2 per MAU, the 11,000 MAU figure) come from the sponsor's platform and are not independently checked in the video. The payout model is a source of uncertainty.
Auto-caption error: the end date reads 'January 2000. 26' in the transcript. The intro gives January 31, 2026.

relevance.why: Apify's actor contract (containerized tool, typed input schema, structured output, published docs and demo) is a marketplace-style packaging of agent tools, loosely related to AgentOS's pluggable tool and skill direction. Weak signal.
relevance.action: Low priority. If AgentOS ever exposes tools or skills to outside developers, compare its manifest and input/output schema against Apify's actor requirements (README, input schema, demo) as a reference shape.

relevance.why: Uses Claude Code with a vendor-supplied prompt, but nothing about checkpointing, harness design, approvals or credentials. Not a meaningful input.
